q: 1. Excessive free lime and excessive magnesia present in the cement make the cement
options: to have very low initial setting time
to have very light compressive strength
explain: Free lime and magnesia hydrate very slowly, causing expansion and cracking after the cement has set, making it 'unsound'.

q: 2. The dry process of manufacturing cement has become obsolete, because...
options: it is difficult to maintain correct proportions
explain: The key indicates 'all of the above', though modern industry actually prefers dry process for energy efficiency; historically, wet process offered better mixing.

q: 3. Rapid hardening cement attains early strength due to
options: larger proportion of lime grounded finer
small proportion of lime grounded finer
presence of excess percentage of gypsum
explain: Increased lime content (higher C3S) and very fine grinding accelerate the hydration rate and early strength.

q: 4. The main ingredients of Portland cement are
explain: Lime and silica together form the two principal ingredients that combine to produce the cementing compounds in Portland cement.

q: 5. Portland cement manufactured from pure white chalk and clay but free from iron oxide, is known as
explain: Iron oxide provides the grey color to cement; by removing it, white cement is produced for architectural use.

q: 6. Le Chatelier's device is used for determining the
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures the expansion of cement paste, which indicates its soundness.

q: 7. Which constituent of the cement, upon a addition of water, sets and hardness first
explain: Tricalcium Aluminate (C3A) is the first compound to react and set upon contact with water.

q: 8. The initial setting time for ordinary Portland cement should not be less than
explain: As per IS specification, OPC must have an initial setting time of not less than 30 minutes to allow adequate working time.

q: 9. The quality of cement is good if it has more of
explain: High C3S content ensures better early strength and binding quality in Portland cement.

q: 10. The maximum final setting time for ordinary Portland cement should be
explain: The final setting time of OPC should not exceed 10 hours as per the specification limit.

q: 11. Quick setting cement is used
options: where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick-setting cement is essential for underwater work where the cement must set before being washed away by currents.

q: 12. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are
explain: Quick setting cement has an initial setting time of 5 minutes and a final setting time of 30 minutes.

q: 13. The pozzolona portland cement gains the strength
explain: PPC gains strength slower than OPC because the pozzolanic reaction takes longer than the primary hydration of cement.

q: 14. Snowcem is
explain: Snowcem is a well-known brand of waterproof cement paint used on exterior masonry surfaces.

q: 15. Compared to the ordinary portland cement, the ultimate strength of the pozzolona portland cement is
explain: While slow to start, PPC eventually achieves a higher ultimate strength due to the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrates.

q: 16. In low heat cement, the proportion of the following compound is kept at low value
explain: Both C3A and C3S produce significant heat; their levels are minimized in low-heat cement to prevent thermal cracking.

q: 17. In the chemical composition of test for loss on ignition, the cement is treated to a temperature of
explain: Loss on ignition involves heating a sample to 900-1000°C until constant weight is reached.

q: 18. Loss on ignition in cement should not exceed
explain: Standard specifications limit Loss on Ignition to a maximum of 4% for OPC.

q: 19. Lime is considered to be hydraulic lime when it sets under water within
explain: Hydraulic lime is defined by its ability to set and harden under water within about 7 to 30 days.

q: 20. The insoluble residues in good cement should be
explain: Insoluble residue indicates the purity of the cement and should be less than 1.5%.

q: 21. During the test of portland cement for “loss of ignition” the loss in weight occurs due to
explain: High temperature drives off moisture and CO2 from carbonates present in the sample.

q: 22. The volume of one bag of cement weighing 50 kg is
explain: Based on a density of 1440 kg/m³, the volume of 50 kg of cement is 50/1440 ≈ 0.0347 m³.

q: 23. Slag cement contains
explain: According to the key, slag cement contains sulphate, though it primarily consists of granulated blast furnace slag.

q: 24. The setting time of concrete is reduced during summer due to
explain: High temperature, wind, and low humidity all accelerate moisture evaporation and hydration, reducing concrete's setting time in summer.

q: 25. If P is the percentage of water required for normal consistency, water to be added for determination of initial setting time is,
explain: For setting time tests, the water content is standardized at 0.85 times the water required for standard consistency.

q: 26. A badly mixed cement concrete results in
explain: Improper mixing leads to air pockets and uneven aggregate distribution known as honeycombing.

q: 27. Strength of cement, with storage
explain: Cement absorbs moisture from the air during storage (pre-hydration), which reduces its bonding strength over time.

q: 28. Storage of cement should be done on
explain: Cement must be kept on a raised, dry platform away from walls to prevent moisture absorption.

q: 29. The cement mortar mix generally used for masonry work
explain: A 1:6 ratio (1 part cement to 6 parts sand) is the standard economical mix for general masonry.

q: 30. Lime used for works under water
explain: Hydraulic lime, capable of setting and hardening under water, is specifically used for underwater construction works.

q: 31. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plaster
explain: For internal plastering, a 1:4 mix (one part cement to four parts sand) is standard as it provides a good balance of workability and strength without excessive shrinkage.

q: 32. The rate of hydration and hydrolysis of cement depends upon its
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area exposed to water, increasing the rate of hydration and hydrolysis.

q: 33. The cement mortar mix generally used for external plaster
explain: External plaster requires high resistance to weathering; a 1:4 mix is typically used to ensure durability and water-tightness.

q: 34. The most commonly used retarder in cement is
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard the fast-setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate.

q: 35. The cement mortar mix generally used for ceiling plaster
explain: Ceiling plaster needs a richer mix (1:3) to provide better adhesion and to counteract the effects of gravity during application.

q: 36. Which of the following cements contains maximum percentage of dicalcium silicate?
explain: Low heat cement contains a higher proportion of slow-hydrating dicalcium silicate (C2S) to reduce heat generation.

q: 37. During Rana Cracy, types of mortar generally used for public buildings are
explain: Historically in Nepal (Rana Era), lime and surkhi (crushed brick) were the primary binding materials before cement became widely available.

q: 38. The most common admixture which is used to accelerate the initial set of concrete is
explain: Calcium chloride is the most widely used accelerator, speeding up the hydration reaction and initial setting of concrete.

q: 39. Vicat's apparatus is used to determine all of the following except
explain: Vicat's apparatus determines consistency and setting times of cement, but fineness modulus is measured separately (via sieve analysis), not by Vicat's apparatus.

q: 40. In the soundness test, the whole assembly is immersed in water for
explain: In the Le Chatelier soundness test, the mould assembly is immersed in water for 24 hours before measuring expansion.

q: 41. The fat lime swells ....... times of its original volume during slaking
explain: Fat lime, being pure and highly reactive, swells to about four to five times its original volume when slaked with water.

q: 42. Gypsum is a
explain: Gypsum is a chemically precipitated sedimentary rock, formed from the evaporation of mineral-rich water.

q: 43. The constituent of cement which is responsible for all the undesirable properties of cement is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) is associated with undesirable properties such as flash setting, high heat of hydration, and poor sulphate resistance.

q: 44. Gypsum consists of
explain: Gypsum is chemically calcium sulfate dihydrate, composed of CaSO4 combined with water (H2O).

q: 45. The most commonly used retarder in cement is (Accelerator: CaCl2, Retarder: Gypsum)
explain: Gypsum is added during clinker grinding specifically to retard the fast setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate.

q: 46. The initial setting time of lime -pozzolana is
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures typically have a longer initial setting time of about 2 hours.

q: 47. A mortar joint in masonry which is normal to the face of wall is known as
explain: A cross joint runs perpendicular (normal) to the face of the wall, connecting adjacent bricks in a course.

q: 48. The proportions of lime and sand in the mortar normally used in brick construction are
explain: A lime to sand ratio of about 1:6 is commonly used in ordinary brick masonry mortar.

q: 49. The seven days compressive strength of a good portland cement, as obtained from the compressive test of cement sand mortar should not be less than
explain: A good Portland cement should achieve a 7-day compressive strength of at least about 175 kg/cm2 in a standard mortar test.

q: 50. The main constituent of a Portland cement is:
explain: Lime is the principal constituent by weight in Portland cement, forming the basis of its cementing compounds.
